concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Primary request: edit the supplied Helmetd motorcycle HUD into a practical COMPACT 3D NAVIGATION MAP concept. Preserve its landscape 16:9 rider-eye road photograph, helmetd wordmark at top left, Wi-Fi icon and 82% battery at top right, original top-center left-turn instruction '800 ft / Oak Street', and fixed bottom-center '32 mph' and '3 GEAR'. Keep the existing restrained white sans-serif and cyan navigation design language.
Add one small, beautifully rendered isometric 3D map in the lower-left quadrant, occupying roughly 28% of image width and 27% height, leaving the entire forward road center open. This is a virtual miniature map tile inside the HUD, not a route painted on the real roadway. The map must look genuinely three-dimensional: low-rise extruded grey/off-white building blocks with visible top and side faces, streets between them, a slight ground-plane tilt, and precise restrained shading. Show a cyan route running forward from a small cyan triangular rider marker, then bending LEFT around a block to agree with the next-turn arrow. Include one small amber reported-hazard pin beside the route. No photographic satellite texture, no giant holographic city, no decorative sci-fi mesh.
Use a very subtle translucent map base with a thin edge and lots of open space; don't make it a dark opaque tablet screen. The clear small header above the miniature map reads 'ROUTE'. A short caption below reads '12 min · 4.2 mi', and an unobtrusive amber sublabel reads '1 reported hazard'. Any map street label is limited to 'Oak St'. The geometry should be readable at a glance with no dense labels or tiny menus.
Remove the existing left-edge camera glyph where the map occupies its space. Retain the right-edge camera glyph and tiny lower-right microphone, but remove the 'Voice ready' caption to reduce clutter. Do not add other alerts.
White presentation footer outside the scene reads exactly 'HELMETD / 3D MINI MAP' at left and 'Motorcycle HUD concept' at right.
Constraints: a polished realistic AR HUD UI design, one coherent screen, exact legible text, map visually secondary to the road and navigation arrow. No device bezel, touch buttons, full-screen map, world-locked pavement arrows, collision predictions, extra numbers, marketing text or neon glow.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Primary request: edit the supplied Helmetd motorcycle HUD into an EXPANDED 3D ROUTE OVERVIEW for a stationary rider planning a route. Preserve its landscape 16:9 rider-eye photographic street background, helmetd wordmark at upper left, Wi-Fi icon and 82% battery at upper right, clean white sans-serif typography and cyan accent. The scene is stationary; no motion blur. Remove the normal navigation arrow, camera icons and Voice ready caption. In the original bottom-center speed/gear position show '0 mph' and '— GEAR'.
The main visual is a premium, clearly three-dimensional isometric miniature street map floating in the center/lower-middle of the HUD, about 55% of image width. Tilt its ground plane so building sides and rooftops are visible, with extruded grey-white low-rise city blocks, a small park with stylized trees, a simplified river edge, precise street grid, and subtle realistic shading. This is a virtual map visualization, not reconstruction of the forward real street and not a route projected onto the pavement. Keep the surrounding road recognizable. Avoid a large opaque rectangular panel.
Top center title exactly 'ROUTE OVERVIEW', with 'Riverside Park' in smaller text below. Through the miniature city show two routes from a small rider marker to a destination pin: selected cyan route gently winding past fewer amber hazard pins; alternate route in muted white dashed line. A tiny cyan group-rider dot labeled 'Riley' may appear on the selected route. Keep map labels extremely sparse and readable.
Beneath the map, above the fixed speed/gear readout, two clean horizontally arranged route-choice blocks with thin dividers rather than heavy cards: left block 'Fastest' and '18 min · 3 reports'; right block 'Fewer reported hazards' and '20 min · 1 report'. Give the right block a thin cyan selection outline. These are illustrative report counts, not a guarantee of road safety.
Place a small noninteractive state label 'STOPPED · ROUTE PLANNING' under the title or at the lower left. No huge button implying touch controls on the glasses, no emergency alert, no turn-signal camera window.
White presentation footer outside the scene reads 'HELMETD / 3D ROUTE OVERVIEW' at left and 'Stationary planning concept' at right.
Constraints: polished high-fidelity product mockup, clearly visible 3D geometry and route paths, typography matching the reference, clean hierarchy. No massive holographic sci-fi city, neon bloom, grids in the sky, street-level augmented arrows, dense map text, developer overlays, extra slogans, web browser chrome or hardware frames.

selected_correction.prompt: Make a single targeted cleanup to this 3D route-overview HUD concept: remove BOTH occurrences of the small white name 'Riley' printed near the cyan route in the center of the miniature map. Keep the small cyan group-position dot but leave it unlabeled. Fill the removed text areas with the underlying map/road geometry. Preserve all other text, every building, both routes, hazard pins, destination label, route comparison controls, background photo, colors, speed, gear, and footer exactly as closely as possible. Do not add or change any other UI.
